votes.corrected_statement: I couldn't refute this; the claim holds at 36dd8ac. On the real verify run path, `verify_pass::mutate` always builds its `MutationRun` with `assertion_flipped: None` (crates/rk-cli/src/verify_pass.rs:667 and :707). So `flip_predicate` returns only MutationSurvived or Unverifiable, never Pinned (crates/rk-kernel/src/verify/flip.rs:64-68). Separately, `verify_step_six` passes `&BTreeMap::new()` as the assertions map to `compute_ledger` (crates/rk-cli/src/verbs/run.rs:4228-4234). `ac_status` gives Pinned or MutationSurvived only when an assertion locator is present (crates/rk-kernel/src/verify/ledger.rs:82-92). Each of the two blocks is enough by itself to stop a pin. Every declared-mutation criterion therefore lands as `unpinned` (not even `mutation_survived`). `stage_exit` accepts only Pinned or HumanAnswered (crates/rk-types/src/artifact/ledger.rs:54-56; crates/rk-kernel/src/verify/exit.rs:44). `ac_gate::answers` counts only non-voided gate answers whose verdict is DISCRIMINATES and that name an answerer (crates/rk-kernel/src/verify/ac_gate.rs:169-209). So a criterion can be closed only by a human "discriminates" answer, never by a mutation pin. One caveat outside the claim: an item with no Spec criteria exits with no human answer, because the ledger is empty (run.rs:4089-4091).

synthesis.process_verdict:
The process is honest and self-correcting but heavy:
- It records its own false passes and runs adversarial review rounds that do find real defects.
- 198 ADRs, 184 decisions and a 50k-line runbook keep the chain of evidence intact.
- The plan grew from 14 to 30 stages in 24 days. Each expansion was triggered by first contact with a real run, which is the right reason, but nothing caps it.
- About 70% of last week's commits changed docs only, and the current stage has added no Rust to this repo.
- The records have drifted: the remote CI campaign of 10-03 never entered them, and several tracker rows are stale.

The operator is now the bottleneck: paid steps cannot run unattended, and 20 rulings await ratification.
recommendations: Today: merge the remote branch locally, push with a go-ahead, iterate until CI is green on Linux and Windows, record the run ids, and correct every 'never pushed / never run' statement.

Start 8j's build work (human roots, hold, lane proofs, fix-item shortlist, exit-check amendments) now, in parallel with S-BIN's paid batches. Keep the pin move and paid probes behind Checkpoint 8i. Expected saving is about 1-3 days.
Before any paid lane run, fix Ctrl-C, make status per-item, add Rust to the tie check, and stop the tests reading Anthropic env vars. This is about a day of agent work.

Move the biggest unknown forward: run the pin move and three confinement probes first, then one real `redkiln run` dispatch on the fixture item before the 20-checkpoint freeze, and write the recovery procedure for a failed first run.
Define M5 precisely: publish a disposition table for the ~50 unscheduled criteria, and state that verify-stage criteria close by human answer and that the review gate is uncalibrated.
Clear the ratification backlog in one sitting: 20 provisional rulings, Record A, the temper baseline, and where the Codex adapter belongs.
After M5, run a 1-2 week hardening and doc-diet pass and cap stage-file size before starting Phase 2.
